As of March 2026, there have been 106<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.india.gov.in/my-government/constitution-india/amendments|title=Amendments {{!}} National Portal of India|website=india.gov.in|access-date=2019-03-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181122212554/https://www.india.gov.in/my-government/constitution-india/amendments|archive-date=22 November 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Amendment of the Constitution of India|amendments of the Constitution of India]] since it was first enacted in 1950.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://indiacode.nic.in/coiweb/coifiles/amendment.htm |title=The Constitution Amendment Acts |publisher=Indiacode.nic.in |access-date=2011-11-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080427052233/http://indiacode.nic.in/coiweb/coifiles/amendment.htm |archive-date=27 April 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The Indian Constitution is one of the most amended national constitutions in the world.<ref name="Krishnamurthy2009">{{cite journal|url=http://www.yale.edu/yjil/files_PDFs/vol34/Krishnamurthy.pdf |page=219 |title=Colonial Cousins: Explaining India and Canada's Unwritten Constitutional Principles |last=Krishnamurthi |first=Vivek |date=2009 |volume=34 |issue=1 |journal=[[Yale Journal of International Law]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304075730/http://www.yale.edu/yjil/files_PDFs/vol34/Krishnamurthy.pdf |archive-date=2016-03-04 }}</ref> The Constitution spells out governmental powers with so much detail that many matters addressed by statute in other democracies must be addressed via constitutional amendment in India. As a result, the Constitution is amended roughly twice a year.

There are three types of amendments to the [[Constitution of India]] of which the second and third types of amendments are governed by [[Amendment of the Constitution of India|Article 368]].

* The first type of amendment must be passed by a "[[Majority|simple majority]]" in each house of the [[Parliament of India]].
* The second type of amendment must be passed by a prescribed "[[Supermajority|special majority]]" of each house of Parliament; and
* The third type of amendment must be passed by a "special majority" in each house of Parliament and ratified by at least one half of the [[State Legislative Assembly (India)|State Legislatures]]. Examples of the third type of amendment include amendments No. 3, 6, 7, 8, 13, 14, 15, 16, 22, 23, 24, 25, 28, 30, 31, 32, 35, 36, 38, 39, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 51, 54, 61, 62, 70, 73, 74, 75, 79, 84, 88, 95, 99, 101, and 104.<ref name="Nature and Scope">{{cite web|title=Constitution Amendment: Nature and Scope of the Amending Process, (page 10)|url=http://164.100.47.134/intranet/CAI/1.pdf|work=Lok Sabha Secretariat|access-date=1 December 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203013055/http://164.100.47.134/intranet/CAI/1.pdf|archive-date=3 December 2013}}</ref>

|| Amendment designed to negate the judgement of [[Allahabad High Court|Allahabad HC]] in ''[[State of Uttar Pradesh v. Raj Narain]]'' 1975 SCR (3) 333 invalidating PM Indira Gandhi's election to parliament. Amendment placed restrictions on judicial scrutiny of post of Prime Minister.<ref>{{cite web |title=HOW THE CONGRESS HAD WRECKED CONSTITUTION |url=http://www.dailypioneer.com/columnists/edit/how-the-congress-had-wrecked-constitution.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304075617/http://www.dailypioneer.com/columnists/edit/how-the-congress-had-wrecked-constitution.html |archive-date=4 March 2016 |access-date=2015-12-09 |publisher=dailypioneer.com}}</ref> Irrespective of electoral malpractice, no case can be filed against president, vice president, speaker of lok sabha and prime minister. 
Later, clauses (4) and (5) of Article 329A were struck down by the Supreme Court in ''[https://api.sci.gov.in/judgment/judis/21398.pdf Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain]'' 1976 (2) SCR 347, for being in violation of basic structure.

| [[Forty-second Amendment of the Constitution of India|42nd]] || Amend articles 31, 31C, 39, 55, 74, 77, 81, 82, 83, 100, 102, 103, 105, 118, 145, 150, 166, 170, 172, 189, 191, 192, 194, 208, 217, 225, 226, 227, 228, 311, 312, 330, 352, 353, 356, 357, 358, 359, 366, 368 and 371F.<br>Insert articles 31D, 32A, 39A, 43A, 48A, 131A, 139A, 144A, 226A, 228A and 257A.<br>Insert parts IVA and XIVA.<br>Amend schedule 7.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://indiacode.nic.in/coiweb/amend/amend42.htm |title=Forty Second Amendment |publisher=Indiacode.nic.in |access-date=2011-11-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150328040620/http://indiacode.nic.in/coiweb/amend/amend42.htm |archive-date=28 March 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> ||  3 January, 1 February & 1 April 1977<ref name="AMENDMENT ACTS"/>
|| Amendment passed during internal emergency by Indira Gandhi. Provides for curtailment of fundamental rights, imposes [[Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles and Fundamental Duties of India|fundamental duties]] and changes to the basic structure of the constitution by making India a "Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic".
However, the Supreme Court, in ''[[Minerva Mills v. Union of India]]''  1980 SCC (3) 625, quashed the amendments to Articles 31C and 368 as it was in contravention with the basic structure of the Constitution.

| [[Forty-fourth Amendment of the Constitution of India|44th]] || Amend articles 19, 22, 30, 31A, 31C, 38, 71, 74, 77, 83, 103, 105, 123, 132, 133, 134, 139A, 150, 166, 172, 192, 194, 213, 217, 225, 226, 227, 239B, 329, 352, 356, 358, 359, 360 and 371F.<br>Insert articles 134A and 361A.<br>Remove articles 31, 257A and 329A.<br>Amend part 12.<br>Amend schedule 9.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://indiacode.nic.in/coiweb/amend/amend44.htm |title=Forty Fourth Amendment |publisher=Indiacode.nic.in |access-date=2011-11-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080621114155/http://indiacode.nic.in/coiweb/amend/amend44.htm |archive-date=21 June 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref> || 20 June, 1 August & 6 September 1979<ref name="AMENDMENT ACTS"/>

| 12 January 2012 
| Added the words "or co-operative societies" after the word "or unions" in Article 19(l)(c) and insertion of article 43B i.e., Promotion of Co-operative Societies and added Part-IXB i.e., The Co-operative Societies. In July 2021 Supreme Court Struck Part of the amendment as it was not ratified by the states.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/sc-quashes-part-of-upa-era-constitutional-amendment-101626804819445.html|title=SC quashes part of UPA-era constitutional amendment|date=20 July 2021}}</ref>

The amendment objective is to encourage economic activities of cooperatives which in turn help progress of rural India. It is expected to not only ensure autonomous and democratic functioning of cooperatives, but also the accountability of the management to the members and other stakeholders.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pib.nic.in/newsite/erelease.aspx?relid=81715|title=Ninety Seventh Amendment (PIB)|access-date=28 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141217045456/http://pib.nic.in/newsite/erelease.aspx?relid=81715|archive-date=17 December 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

|style="background:#e6e6e6" | Formation of a [[National Judicial Appointments Commission]]. 16 State assemblies out of 29 States including [[Goa]], [[Rajasthan]], [[Tripura]], [[Gujarat]] and [[Telangana]] ratified the Central Legislation, enabling the President of India to give assent to the bill.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jagranjosh.com/current-affairs/16-states-ratified-national-judicial-appointments-commission-bill-2014-1419859039-1|title=16 States ratified National Judicial Appointments Commission Bill, 2014|date=29 December 2014|website=Jagranjosh.com|access-date=2 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618131346/https://www.jagranjosh.com/current-affairs/16-states-ratified-national-judicial-appointments-commission-bill-2014-1419859039-1|archive-date=18 June 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> The amendment was struck down by the Supreme Court on 16 October 2015.
